title: Deployed Math, Light, and Judgment Reveal Misalignment
claim: Correctly deployed mathematics, using accurate inputs and an appropriate model, reliably exposes numerical or structural misalignment. In that limited sense it is analogous to light and to judgment: a standard exists, an actual state is compared with the standard, misalignment is exposed, and consequences follow. The theological bridge claim is that divine judgment performs a deeper version of this structure in the moral and personal domain.
assumptions: A stable comparison standard exists in the domain under review.
The actual state can be represented with enough fidelity for comparison.
The mathematical model, units, and operations are appropriate to the target domain.
For the theological bridge, moral and personal alignment are meaningful categories not reducible to arithmetic.
definitions: Deployed mathematics: mathematics applied to a concrete state through a specified model and input set.
Exposure of misalignment: the disclosure of discrepancy between a state and a standard.
Judgment pattern: standard, actual state, comparison, exposed alignment or misalignment, and consequence.
bridges: divine judgment -> moral and personal exposure
negative_guards: Do not claim mathematics itself makes moral judgments.
Do not claim arithmetic establishes guilt, motive, or mercy.
Do not claim the analogy becomes identity across all properties.
Do not treat correct arithmetic with wrong inputs as truth exposure.
Do not promote beyond C3 without a formal preservation map for the relevant relations.
kill_conditions: The pattern cannot preserve standard, state, comparison, exposure, and consequence across the compared domains.
A counterexample shows the relevant mathematics hides rather than exposes discrepancy under accurate inputs and a fitting model.
The theological bridge requires moral properties that cannot be mapped without adding unrelated assumptions.
A rival reading explains the same examples as mere metaphor with no preserved structure.
